summary.headline: TVS SCS Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record Rs 3,687 crore (+38.5% YoY) and PBT doubled to Rs 50.6 crore; management targets 20%+ FY27 revenue growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 38.5% YoY to Rs 3,687 crore, with both ISCS (+24.8%) and GFS (+79.1%) growing and India up 64.1%. Consolidated EBITDA rose 50.2% to a 7.3% margin, and PBT more than doubled to Rs 50.6 crore (1.4% margin). Growth was partly driven by freight rate increases, and gross debt rose Rs 140 crore on working capital. Management reiterated 20%+ FY27 growth, doubling FY27 operating PBT versus FY26, and a 4% PBT margin by Q4 FY28.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 24.4 crore in Q2 FY26 and Rs 32.1 crore in Q1 FY27
vs 8.7% in Q2 FY26 and 8.1% in Q1 FY27
vs 2.2% in Q2 FY26 and 4.1% in Q1 FY27

segments.name: ISCS (Integrated Supply Chain Solutions)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 2,488 crore (+24.8% YoY); EBITDA margin 9.2%, up 50 bps YoY, driven by business mix and new business. H1 revenue Rs 4,905 crore (+23.4%).

segments.name: GFS (Global Forwarding Solutions)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 1,199 crore (+79.1% YoY); EBITDA margin 3.9%, versus 2.2% a year ago and 4.1% in Q1. Management says about two-thirds of growth came from volume, not rates. H1 revenue Rs 2,117 crore (+65.5%).

segments.name: India geography
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 64.1% YoY, with ISCS up 36% and GFS growth in renewables and automobiles up 136%. Management said India margins are better than the group average, without giving figures.

segments.name: Rest of world
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 29% YoY, with ISCS up 21% and GFS up 55%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 20%+ across both segments; management said GFS may not repeat 70-80% growth in H2 but expects greater than 20% for the next two quarters.
FY27 operating PBT to double versus FY26 operating profit of about Rs 97 crore, implying about Rs 200 crore; H1 FY27 operating PBT was about Rs 83 crore.
GFS EBITDA margin aspiration of 4.5-5%, with FY28 as the target and possibly Q4 FY27 as a stretch.
Group PBT margin target of 4% by Q4 FY28; reaching it needs 150-200 bps ISCS margin improvement, from 9.2% toward 10.5-11%.
FY28 ISCS growth aspiration of high-teens or mid-teens, with no formal forecast given.
ALA MENA JV expected to start generating revenue in Q4 FY27; Sankyu partnership expected to have a P&L impact in FY28. Effective tax rate guided at about 30% and stable.
capex_capacity: ALA JV with ALA MENA (51% TVS SCS / 49% ALA MENA) is operational; share allotment approved by the board on 6 October 2026 and EN 9120:2018 warehouse certification obtained for aerospace and defence work.
Depreciation rose to Rs 166 crore in Q2 (Rs 137 crore YoY) and lease interest to Rs 27 crore (Rs 15 crore YoY), driven by a new Northern America project started in H2 FY26.
Swamy & Sons 3PL, acquired in May 2026 and fully funded from internal accruals, is margin accretive on EBITDA and PBT and adds warehousing capacity in India.
Management said it is building capacity where required, but gave no capex figure.
demand_pricing: Business development pipeline of Rs 8,200 crore, up from Rs 7,500 crore at end-Q1 and Rs 6,100 crore at March 2026.
New business revenue exceeded Rs 500 crore for the third consecutive quarter (Rs 523 crore in Q2).
Europe contract renewals of 2-10 year duration; several large, long-term European wins in ISCS.
Freight costs rose to Rs 1,287 crore (Rs 727 crore YoY), largely from GFS volume growth; management said the rate environment is outside its control and some capacity is hard to get.
Sankyu Inc. (Japan) MOU signed in August 2026; Sankyu intends to acquire 0.5% equity in TVS SCS, pending regulatory approval (filed, not yet received).

qa_highlights.question: How is the company managing freight-rate downside risk in GFS, and how are large contracts kept on schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about two-thirds of GFS growth came from volume rather than rates. Large projects are tracked by a dedicated team supervised by the MD and CFO, with leading KPIs.

qa_highlights.question: How is working capital and debt managed as revenue scales, and how is net margin improved?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about Rs 234 crore of cash was generated in the current year and reinvested. Gross debt rose Rs 140 crore for working capital, with DSO and DPO monitored. Management said most customers are Fortune 500 firms, so receivable risk is limited.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in ISCS growth, and will mid-20s growth continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is broad-based across India, Europe and the US, with new Europe contracts and a US project now generating revenue. Management is confident of 20%+ ISCS growth in FY27 and aspires to high-teens or mid-teens in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What structural changes drive GFS, and what happens to margins if freight rates fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Changes are regional empowerment, lane optimisation and supplier consolidation. Management said margins should hold because of operating leverage, and it targets 4.5-5% GFS margin from 3.9%.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be FX gains or losses to forecast?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FX impact comes mainly from GFS multi-country trade, not from local-currency operations in Europe and the US, and is hedged; it is not forecastable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 profit target and the path to 4% PBT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 operating PBT should double from about Rs 97 crore to about Rs 200 crore. The 4% PBT margin is targeted for Q4 FY28, requiring ISCS margin to rise 150-200 bps.

risks_watch: GFS margin is sensitive to freight rates and volume mix; management could not give rate-sensitivity figures.
Forex line items are volatile and sizeable relative to PBT; the CFO said they cannot be forecast.
Working capital and debt rising with growth; net profit margin is thin at about 1%.
ALA JV revenue timing (Q4 FY27) depends on tri-party agreements and aerospace and defence sales cycles; Sankyu's investment awaits regulatory approval.
Effective tax rate of about 30% limits PAT conversion.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and the pipeline, with explicit targets for FY27 and FY28. More measured on GFS rate sensitivity, FX and the timing of the ALA and Sankyu partnerships, which management said will matter mainly from FY28.
key_quotes: I am very pleased to report our highest ever quarterly revenue of Rs. 3,687 crores, a year-on-year growth of 38%.
In fact, we are only looking at further improving the margins from 3.9% where it is to 4.5% to 5%.
We are committed to 4% PBT that we had earlier mentioned, and we should be reaching that in the last quarter of FY28.
The effective tax rate is about 30%, and it will be stable.

adds.what: Swamy & Sons 3PL acquisition adding warehousing capacity in India (acquired May 2026, funded from internal accruals; capacity size not quantified)
ALA MENA JV (51% stake) operational; expected to start generating revenue in Q4 FY27

growth.why: Management targets 20%+ FY27 revenue growth across ISCS (>20%) and GFS, backed by a Rs 8,200 crore BD pipeline and Rs 523 crore new business in Q2, but no capex figure or specific new capacity size was given and GFS growth is expected to slow in H2.

oneOffs.what: Forex line items are volatile and sizeable relative to PBT (CFO says not forecastable); no specific Q2 FY27 or base-quarter amount given in brief

quality.why: Revenue grew 38.5% to Rs 3,687 cr, with GFS +79.1% about two-thirds from volume (not rates) and ISCS +24.8% broad-based, so growth is largely recurring; however, freight pass-through in GFS inflates top-line growth and the brief gives no quantified one-offs, leaving the verdict mixed rather than fully sustainable.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Group EBITDA margin 7.3% (+60 bps YoY) and PBT margin target of 4% by Q4 FY28 needs ISCS margin up 150-200 bps from 9.2% to 10.5-11%, with GFS margin aiming 4.5-5% from 3.9%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Swamy & Sons 3PL (acquired May 2026) adds Indian warehousing and ALA MENA JV starts revenue in Q4 FY27, but no capacity size or capex figure was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets 20%+ FY27 growth across ISCS and GFS, backed by a Rs 8,200 crore BD pipeline (up from Rs 6,100 crore in March 2026) and Rs 523 crore new business in Q2; GFS growth expected to slow in H2 but stay above 20% for the next two quarters.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is building capacity where required but gave no capex figure and no utilisation level was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth target already raised to 20%+ and H1 revenue grew 33.6% to Rs 7,022 crore, but H2 GFS growth is expected to slow from 79% in Q2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: GFS margin is freight-rate and volume-mix sensitive, freight costs rose to Rs 1,287 crore (vs Rs 727 crore YoY), and FX line items are volatile and cannot be forecast relative to PBT of Rs 50.6 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products or service lines were discussed beyond ALA MENA JV revenue starting Q4 FY27 and Sankyu partnership impact in FY28.

rows.label: ALA MENA JV revenue start
rows.why: 51%-owned JV is operational and guided to start generating revenue in Q4 FY27, though timing depends on tri-party agreements and aerospace/defence sales cycles.

rows.label: Business development pipeline Rs 8,200 cr
rows.why: Pipeline rose from Rs 7,500 crore at end-Q1 and Rs 6,100 crore at March 2026, with new business above Rs 500 crore for the third straight quarter (Rs 523 crore in Q2).

rows.label: Working capital and debt build
rows.why: Gross debt rose Rs 140 crore for working capital and net margin is only about 1%, so cash conversion is a watch item as revenue scales.

tone.note: Management was confident on 20%+ FY27 growth, the Rs 8,200 crore pipeline and the FY27 PBT doubling to about Rs 200 crore; it was measured on GFS freight-rate sensitivity, FX, and the ALA and Sankyu timing.
